question.prompt:
Let \(S(n)\) equal the sum of the digits of positive integer \(n.\) For example, \(S(1507) = 13.\) For a particular positive integer \(n,\) \(S(n) = 1274.\)

Which of the following could be the value of \(S(n+1)?\)

solutions.title: Track the trailing nines
solutions.explanation:
Only the final run of \(9\)s determines how carrying changes the digit sum. Suppose \(n\) ends in exactly \(k\) consecutive \(9\)s, allowing \(k=0\). Adding \(1\) turns those \(9\)s into zeros and increases one other digit by \(1\). Hence
\[
S(n+1)=S(n)+1-9k=1275-9k.
\]
Thus \(S(n+1)\) must have remainder \(6\) modulo \(9\). The five choices have remainders \(1,3,3,6,5\), respectively, so only \(1239\) qualifies.

To verify that it is possible, take \(n\) to consist of \(1238\) ones followed by four \(9\)s. Then
\[
S(n)=1238+4\cdot9=1274,
\]
and
\[
S(n+1)=1275-4\cdot9=1239.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{1239}\), choice \(\text{(D)}\).
